body: claimed: research agent (claude-opus-5-5) · 2026-11-15T20:42Z · worktree/branch none · plan: research

Research answers for #2007 (source trace on main d1484f02a). No code changed.

## 1. File formats: what changes, and is it breaking?

Today:
- `crates/app/src/project/file.rs:97` has `PROJECT_VERSION = 61`. `ToolDto` (L316-422) keeps `holder_d` and `holder_len` (L345-346), `material_group` as free text (L347), and one `rpm` and `feed`.
- `cutting_data: Vec<CuttingRowDto>` (L407-408) holds the rows for each material. It was added with no version step.
- `crates/tools/src/cutting.rs:60-67`: `WorkMaterial` has 6 values and no `Unknown`.
- `crates/app/src/project/cutting_rows_dto.rs` refuses an unknown material word by name.
- `.camtools` (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs:31-33`) is `FORMAT "camcraft-tools"`, `VERSION 1`. The reader refuses each other version (L110-113).
- A library holder is not referenced. `SetToolBody::library` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs:155-169`) copies the outline into the tool as a drawn spun body.

Decision (recommended option taken):
- Add `WorkMaterial::Unknown` (word `unknown`).
- On load, the old `rpm`/`feed` of a tool become its `Unknown` row. The old rows stay as they are.
- Add a tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` that references a library entry by name.
- An old drawn library copy and an old `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder load as a custom holder, with no change to the shape.
- This is a version step: `PROJECT_VERSION` 61 to 62, and `.camtools` `VERSION` 1 to 2. The new readers read the old versions and migrate them.
- An older build refuses the new file (a word it does not know). Thus the PRs that write the new keys are `feat!` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- Dropped: additive keys with no version step. An old build then reads `unknown` as a bad file, or drops the holder reference silently. A silent drop is not permitted.

## 2. Collision and simulation: one holder shape

Today the one seam is `crates/app/src/tool_body.rs`:
- `judged()` L173-188: with no body, the laws read the tool's own holder cylinder. With a body, the holder is widened by `HolderProfile::enclose`. A machine-default body is floored at the parameter cylinder (#828).
- `stack()` L193-195 gives the band stack for the fixture laws. `digest()` L200 is the stamp term.
- The callers: `operation/tool_gate.rs:248`, `machine/mod.rs:201`, `posting_index_swing.rs:340`, `fixture_struck.rs:46,59`, `operation/generate.rs:100,3116`, `generate/run_job.rs:72`, `kept_rejudge.rs:57,110`, `operation/body_judged.rs:24`, `sim_tool_body.rs:196-197`.

Decision: keep this one seam. Resolve the library reference to a `HolderProfile` in `judged`, `stack` and `digest`. The preview (`draw_tool_preview`) and the simulation (`sim_tool_body.rs`) read the same resolved shape. The #828 floor stays for a machine default (#2009 shows it). This work is under the safety floor: `effort:max`.

## 3. How the work material is selected

Today:
- The material is one value for the document: the singleton `WorkMaterialDef` (`crates/app/src/schema.rs:674-679`), read by `cutting::material_of` (`crates/app/src/cutting.rs:28`).
- `SetWorkMaterial` (`crates/app/src/commands/cutting_data.rs:30-92`) sets it and reseeds the tools and operations in one undo step.
- The setup stock (`StockShape`, `StockDto` in `file.rs`) has no material.
- `row_for` (`crates/tools/src/cutting_rows.rs:26`) gives `None` for a material with no row. Then the tool's own `rpm`/`feed` apply. The post reads `Tool::rpm`.
- The rows hold rpm and feed only. Stepdown and stepover rows do not exist.

Decision: the material comes from the setup stock (a new optional field), then from the document material, then `Unknown`. A row gives rpm, feed, stepdown and stepover. A missing value falls back to the `Unknown` row. The rows move numbers only inside commands (the law in `crates/app/src/cutting_rows.rs`: nothing runs on load). Dropped: a material only for the document (the request names the stock), and a material for each operation (it is not in the request).

## 4. Layout: join with #2002 or a separate dialog?

Today `tool_editor_window` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs:594-893`) is a modal window with 3 columns:
- Column 1 (L625-846) puts each label above its input (`field(ui, "Diameter")` then `num(...)`).
- Column 2 is `draw_tool_preview` (L847-851).
- Column 3 is `tool_profile_page::third_column` (L852-856). Its Body tab has `tool_body_page::preview_3d`, which is the second preview. Its Profile tab has the spun table and `tool_holder_picker::holder_picker`.

Decision: join with #2002. The tool settings go into Properties as a property grid with the labels to the left (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/form.rs`, `fields.rs`). The groups are Geometry, Holder, Cutting data and Catalog. One side preview stays in that page. The modal window retires, and with it the cause of #2003. Dropped: a new separate dialog. It gives a second tool editor next to #2002.

## Holders: "a weldon is a weldon"

`crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs` has one Weldon entry for each bore and each taper (`METRIC_BORES` 6/8/10/12/16/20 and `INCH_BORES`, L286-296, `library()` L306-341). `fits_shank` (L220-229) already refuses a wrong shank by name.

Decision: show one "Weldon" entry for each taper. The bore and the body diameter come from the standard bore table by the tool's shank diameter. A shank with no standard bore is refused by name. A real Weldon holder has a fixed bore. Thus the data keeps one bore for each holder, and only the picker changes. Dropped: one Weldon shape that fits each shank. That shape does not exist, and a wrong body diameter changes the collision check.

The sub-issues follow in the next comment.

The research is complete. The answers are in the comment above. The sub-issues are filed (each is `P3`, `enhancement`, `source:agent`, `area:ui`):

| Order | Issue | Effort | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #2014 Tool settings in Properties: a property grid, labels to the left | `effort:medium` | #2002 |
| 2 | #2015 Cutting data by work material: `Unknown` default row, stepdown, stepover, material from the setup stock | `effort:high` (posted feeds and speeds) | none |
| 3 | #2017 One side preview that draws the checked holder shape | `effort:medium` | #2005, #2014 |
| 4 | #2016 Holders reference a library entry; collision, simulation and preview read one shape (`area:sim`) | `effort:max` (collision shape) | none; after #2014 is better |
| 5 | #2018 One Weldon entry for each taper, the bore from the shank (`area:sim`) | `effort:high` (collision shape) | #2016 |

Merge and split decisions:
- "Holders filled from the library" and "the holder fit is not sized for each tool" are one issue (#2016). The two have one cause: `SetToolBody::library` copies the outline and keeps no reference.
- "A weldon is a weldon" is a separate issue (#2018). It changes the picker and the bore selection, and it needs the reference of #2016 first.
- #2015 and #2016 both change the file format. The first to merge takes the version step (`PROJECT_VERSION` 62, `.camtools` 2). The second takes the next step if necessary.

Related, not changed: #2003 (the modal window retires in #2014), #2009 (the machine-default floor display), #808 (no silent holder fallback).

This umbrella closes now. Pick takes only the sub-issues for code.
